summary: Reported nearly finished in 1928 as a 48 ft tower near Waldron; a page marks it removed in 1974, but sources conflict on the county.

facts.status_note: Central US Lookouts lists the White Oak Mountain tower in Scott County as removed in 1974. No other source confirms this, and the same page's 1971 station description places a different steel tower in Franklin County.

events.note: Harrison Times item of October 5, 1928 reported the 48-foot tower as nearing completion; the completion year is not stated.
U.S. Forest Service station description of an 85-foot steel tower with a metal cabin, placed in Franklin County; not confirmed as the same tower as the Scott County entry.
Page entry reads 1974: Removed for the White Oak Mountain tower in Scott County.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Unresolved. The Central US Lookouts page puts the 1928 tower in Scott County, and the OpenStreetMap node sits at the Scott County spot. The page's 1971 station description places a steel tower in Franklin County, with a different position relative to Clarksville, Ozark and Altus. The story reports both and does not merge them.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict. Central US Lookouts describes a 48-foot tower on White Oak Mountain in Scott County, reported nearly finished in October 1928, and marks it removed in 1974. The same page's 1971 station description is for an 85-foot steel tower in Franklin County, and the page does not say whether it is the same structure. The OpenStreetMap node (the brief's coordinates) still exists as an observation tower with a location-check note, and no source found describes the site today. TopoQuest and AnyPlaceAmerica list a White Oak Lookout Tower in Scott County at about 2214 ft, but those pages were not fetched and are not cited. The brief's status was unknown; facts.status is set to removed from the single 1974 entry, with the conflict recorded in status_note, so the editor should confirm before publishing. Confidence low.
